description: Accelerate sync-point discovery using bitvector operations. Instead of decoding symbols one at a time to find where probes converge, use a single pass that marks all possible symbol-start positions in a bitvector, then use fast bitwise operations (popcount, CTZ) to find convergence. This leverages 64-bit word operations to process 64 bit-positions simultaneously.
mathematical_formalization: Create bitvector V of length L. V[i] = 1 iff position i could be a valid symbol start. Initialize: V = all 1s for first max_len positions. Propagate: for each i where V[i]=1, set V[i + decode_length(i)] = 1. Sync point = smallest j > start where popcount(V[j-max_len+1..j]) == 1.
analogical_connections: Bloom filters: compact bitvector probabilistic set membership
Sieve of Eratosthenes: mark composites in a bit array
implementation_hypothesis: Allocate a bitvector of block_size bits. Forward-scan marking reachable bit positions. Use POPCNT to count active probes in 64-bit windows. When only one active probe remains, we've found a sync point.
experiment_seed: Benchmark bitvector-based sync finding vs iterative probe convergence on DEFLATE blocks of varying sizes. Measure time to find first sync point.
